name: Rivian
author: kayleg
description: Your Rivian in the bar: where it is, how full it is, and how far that gets you

barWidget.description: Your Rivian in the bar: where it is, how full it is, and how far that gets you

schema.label: VIN
schema.description: Which car, when the account has more than one. Empty picks the first one Rivian lists, which is the right answer for almost everybody. `bin/rivian vehicles` prints the VINs on the account.

schema.label: Units
schema.description: Rivian reports metric on the wire whatever the car's own screen shows, and does not say which the screen is set to, so there is nothing to follow and this has to be asked. Auto reads your locale, which is right for almost everybody.

schema.label: Map
schema.description: Auto follows your theme: a light theme gets Esri's light grey canvas, a dark one gets the dark. Both are deliberately quiet, which is why they beat OpenStreetMap's own standard style here — that one is the map everybody recognises, and considerably louder behind a marker.

schema.label: Zoom
schema.description: 16 shows the street the car is on and the ones either side, which is the level at which you can tell whether it is where you left it. Lower to see which town, higher to see which parking space.

schema.label: Panel width
schema.description: In the shell's spacing units. The map is this wide and everything else is measured off it, so this one number sizes the whole panel. Anything wider than the screen is trimmed to fit.

schema.label: Look the position up by name
schema.description: Turns the coordinates into a street and a town, through OpenStreetMap's Nominatim. Answers are cached per position, so a parked car is one lookup however often you look at it. Off if you would rather nothing but Rivian learned where the car is.

schema.label: Check on the car every
schema.description: Minutes. Rivian answers this from its own cloud and the car is never involved, so this costs the battery nothing at any interval — it is politeness to Rivian's gateway and nothing more. It is what lights the bar icon.

schema.label: Where a click on the map goes
schema.description: The address opened when you click the map, with {lat} and {lon} standing in for the position. Google Maps by default because that is what most people navigate with; https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat={lat}&mlon={lon}#map=17/{lat}/{lon} keeps it in OpenStreetMap.
